hints: Focus on what is present at time zero, only X and Y are mixed, so think about which reaction can happen first.
Notice how the forward rate must start high then fall as X and Y are used up, while the reverse rate must start at zero then rise as Z forms.
Remember that dynamic equilibrium means both reactions still continue at exactly the same non-zero rate, so look for the curves meeting and flattening together.
walkthrough:
**Think about the starting mixture**

At time = 0, only X and Y are present and no Z has formed yet. So the forward reaction can go fast, but the reverse reaction cannot happen at all.

$$\text{X} + \text{Y} \rightleftharpoons \text{Z}$$

**Follow how the rates change**

As X and Y are used up, their concentration falls, so the rate of the forward reaction decreases. As Z builds up, its concentration rises, so the rate of the reverse reaction increases from zero.

**Apply the rule for dynamic equilibrium**

Gradually the two rates approach each other. At equilibrium they become equal and stay constant at a value above zero, because both reactions continue. That is two curves starting apart, then meeting to form one flat line.

options.A: Both rates level off but at different values, with forward above reverse. At dynamic equilibrium the forward and reverse rates must be exactly equal, so this cannot be correct.
options.B: Both rates fall to zero and the reverse rate goes up then down. This suggests the reactions stop, which is the misconception that equilibrium is static. In dynamic equilibrium rates are equal and non-zero.
options.C: Forward rate starts high and decreases, reverse rate starts at zero and increases, then they meet and stay constant together. This perfectly shows rates becoming equal and continuing in dynamic equilibrium.
options.D: The curves cross but then the forward rate falls to zero while the reverse stays high. This would mean only the reverse reaction continues, so rates are never equal and steady. It confuses equilibrium with completion of the reverse reaction.
